title: Kaja
dek: A Pristinian Elder who argues for income-based taxes, resists concentrated control, cares for Magda and works for a shared defense with the adventurers.

body:
Kaja is a Pristinian Elder who argues with her fellow councillors, supports adventurers without excusing every mistake, and spends time on the ordinary care that public office requires. She opposes Hiram’s preferred financial rescue, helps Magda when the work becomes difficult, and later stands again for election.

A different answer to the crisis

During the Elders’ financial debate, Kaja says the adventurers tried to help and that the consequences were unintended. She defends the existing laws and asks for alternatives to handing control to a select few. Her answer challenges the proposed solution without denying that the financial problem exists.

Institutional continuity

She appears among the Elders and supports Magda as they return to announce a split decision. Later Hawthorne names Kaja and Hiram as candidates running again after giving up their seats for a full election. Candidacy is preserved without inventing that election’s result or a later term of office.

Recorded scenes

  • Opposing concentrated control
  • Kaja supports Magda
  • Hawthorne names the returning candidates

Taxes, frustration and a different answer

At her first recorded assembly Kaja rises slowly with a neighbor’s help and observes that wisdom is often recognized only after it was needed. During the later debt crisis, her position is more specific: she has favored taxes before and still favors them, ideally based on income. She acknowledges the risks adventurers take while arguing that their much larger earnings justify carrying more of the burden.

She is visibly frustrated when Hiram leans across her to talk with Magda, and angrier still when their discussion turns to tea and biscuits while the town’s future is being decided. When the Elders return with their rejection of the business proposal, she supports Magda, smiling and crying. Her opposition has a recorded result, but the scene does not reveal every detail of their private deliberation.

Care for Magda and caution about contamination

At the Common Man, Kaja invites nearby adventurers into a discussion of the town’s supply problems. She wants a way to replace lost access to magical equipment, but firmly rejects bringing dangerous Delerium into Pristinia or near its water. Her account of the earlier cloud and the cause she suspects remains her recollection; it does not replace the quest-established history of that crisis.

She also raises the possibility that Magda should step down for her health, explicitly saying that she has not yet decided on that course. When Magda becomes confused, Kaja corrects a misheard name gently, guides her hand to her tea and helps take her home. Political disagreement with the older woman does not prevent this care. The conversation records concern and assistance, without diagnosing Magda or establishing a resignation.

A shared defense and a boundary on law

As war threatens, Kaja tells the Public Square that townsfolk and adventurers are vulnerable together. She does not require the visitors to be paragons before defending them. After consulting Hiram, she offers to discuss assistance and exchange with the Ahau emissary. Melian then makes the formal request with the council’s approval.

The work also includes the less stirring problem of what to do with the dead. Kaja arranges a meeting with Phelps, brings people in out of the rain and is shocked by the burial bill. A rift interrupts the discussion before a final arrangement is established. In a separate legal discussion she insists that Pristinia cannot enforce its laws beyond the settlement, even when the story being heard is distressing.

At the later election gathering she supports candidacies and joins the votes on eligibility. Hawthorne identifies her as standing again after giving up her seat for the full contest. This history ends with her recorded candidacy and participation, rather than an invented election result.
